verdict.rationale: Checkout.com offers building blocks for event-driven automation — webhooks that fire on payment/dispute/balance events (cko-supp-webhooks) and configurable fraud 'risk rules and lists' that trigger actions on transaction events (checkout-com-docs-28) — but there is no documented general-purpose rules/workflow engine letting users define arbitrary 'if event X then action Y' automations across the platform. Missing for 10: a dedicated no-code/low-code rules builder for arbitrary trigger-action automation, evidence of chained multi-step automation, and any AI-native interface for authoring such rules.
